denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 19318 (bilateral reduction mammaplasty) with date of service 2026-03-23. CARC 96: Non-covered charge(s). RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: The procedure was determined to be cosmetic and is excluded from coverage.

criteria.text: Symptoms attributable to macromastia documented for at least 12 months, such as neck, shoulder, or upper back pain, shoulder grooving, or inframammary intertrigo.
At least 6 months of conservative treatment, including a supportive garment plus physical therapy, analgesics, or dermatologic treatment of intertrigo, without adequate relief.
Estimated resection of at least 500 grams per breast.
Photographic documentation of macromastia and shoulder grooving.

chart.text: Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

30 year old woman here about her breasts, referred by her primary. Exam: large pendulous breasts, nipple to notch 36 on the right and 37 on the left, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both inframammary folds. Discussed reduction, risks, scars, sensation, the works. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies. Surgeries: appendix years ago. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works from home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Going on 24 months of upper back and neck pain that she ties to the weight of the breasts, worse by the end of a shift. Shoulder grooving from the straps, recurrent intertrigo in the folds. She has been in a fitted supportive bra from the specialty shop for months, takes ibuprofen most days, treats the rash with nystatin powder. I am sending her to PT for posture and scapular work. She is 5 foot 3, 163 pounds, which puts BSA right around 1.81. Schnur 22nd percentile at that BSA is about 451 grams. I am estimating 648 grams on the right and 601 on the left.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Eval for upper back and neck pain in the setting of large breasts. Forward shoulder posture, tight pecs, weak lower traps. Plan 8 weeks, twice a week, scapular stabilization and postural retraining.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Blood pressure check. 144 over 90 today, 149 over 84 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 6. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Session 7. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
A1c came back 6.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Back to go over the plan. Symptoms unchanged. We went through the operation again and she wants to proceed if insurance will cover it. Vitals today 116 over 89, pulse 73. Finished 8 weeks of PT across the street, says it helped while she was there and then right back to baseline. Still in the supportive bra, still on the ibuprofen, intertrigo treated with nystatin powder with partial relief. That is 10 months of conservative measures without durable relief.
Standard pre-op photo series taken today, front, both obliques, both laterals. Grooving visible at both shoulders in the AP view, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both folds.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 219, LDL 148, HDL 56, triglycerides 210. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Pre-op visit. Consent signed, marked the plan on her in the mirror, superomedial pedicle, Wise pattern. Labs fine. Stop the ibuprofen a week out.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 96 denial can be answered from the record.
